component.name: Porthole
component.summary: Open a port to your local network, temporarily and on purpose

description.p: On a laptop, exposing a dev server to the local network is usually an all-or-nothing choice: either every high port is reachable by anyone on the network, or reaching your own dev server from your phone means remembering firewall syntax and undoing it again by hand.

Porthole opens a single port towards the network you are on right now, for a bounded amount of time, and closes it again by itself. Opening towards your own network authenticates once per session; opening towards everyone your machine can reach asks every time, because it is the more significant choice. Nothing Porthole opens survives a reboot, and no timed opening can last longer than eight hours.
Porthole is not a firewall manager. It does not do zones, services, NAT, port forwarding or permanent rules — for that, use firewall-config, ufw or nft directly.

screenshot.caption: What is open now, and what is listening on this machine

description.p: First release. Opens a single port towards the local network, or forwards one to a container, for a bounded time, and closes it again by itself. Command line, GTK4 window and desktop notifications; firewalld, ufw or nftables underneath. Packaging for RPM, deb and Arch is in the source tree, and no distribution ships it yet.
